about: Adaptive simulated students (grades 9-12) for the sine in right triangles mission (TUNE-3). Same card format and how_to_use rules as tests/fixtures/students/a_tri.json. Every line is original; no real student text. Four cards: annoyed_obvious, deep_why_stuck, quick_user, misuser.

personas.who: Says everything in one text, including the stuff everyone knows, and hates being asked it again.
personas.style: lowercase, terse, a little smug, no apostrophes
personas.first_text: same angles means same shape, just zoomed. both sides scale so opposite over hypotenuse stays the same, sin 30 is always 0.5. so a 10 ft ramp at 30 rises 5 ft

asks_why: bc if u zoom a photo the angles stay the same, its the same shape
asks_example: a 4 ft rise on an 8 ft ramp, still .5
asks_check_number: yes it stays 0.5, the angles dont change
nudge_hint: ohh like blowing up a photo. the angles dont change
after_quiz_miss: no wait. 6 over 12 is still .5, both sides double
so the sine never changes with size
default: 3/6 and 6/12 are both a half. both sides double so it cancels

expect.asks_obvious: any ask about a given or use idea the first text already covered (or a bare why after a reason) is an annoying move
expect.watch_for: The first text covers the whole lesson. Best Pip says ready or asks one new case. Any re-ask or 'why' on a use/given idea costs the session.

expect.watch_for: Pip must bring the picture (a yes/no concrete case) rather than ask an open why twice. 'idk' twice in a row means Pip failed.

misconception.label: Applies the idea the wrong way with a confident rule
misconception.when: first text. A good Pip files it (heal) and later misses a quiz item because of it; after_quiz_miss lines then re-teach it.

expect.watch_for: Pip files the wrong rule as the kid's rule (no 'that's wrong' lecture), tries it out loud on a case, and the re-teach round K.O.s.
